description: How the internal enterprise roles relate to each other: the board sets targets and capital, functions hand work and pipeline across boundaries, controls gate spend and deals, and operating signals roll back up to leadership.

relationTypes.name: Commercial
relationTypes.description: Internal commissioning of services, platforms, and demand

relationTypes.name: Operational
relationTypes.description: Day-to-day handoffs, approvals, and service delivery between functions

relationTypes.name: Financial
relationTypes.description: Budget allocation, spend control, and capital deployment

relationTypes.name: Information
relationTypes.description: Targets, forecasts, risk signals, and performance feedback

relations.name: Sets growth targets
relations.description: Hands revenue targets, coverage expectations, and forecast cadence to the revenue organization as the frame for pipeline and quota planning.

relations.name: Funds the technology portfolio
relations.description: Allocates capital to product engineering, platform, and tooling investments based on where technology spend creates operating leverage.

relations.name: Reports the forecast
relations.description: Rolls pipeline health and committed forecast up to the CEO and board as the revenue line of the single operating picture.

relations.name: Hands off qualified pipeline
relations.description: Passes qualified demand to sales with full campaign and intent context so sellers pick up opportunities without re-discovery.

relations.name: Feeds back conversion outcomes
relations.description: Returns opportunity progression, win/loss, and revenue attribution so marketing can shift budget toward the demand sources that actually close.

relations.name: Gates deals through controls
relations.description: Reviews non-standard terms, discounts, and contractual exposure in the deal-approval path so revenue closes without creating legal or margin risk.

relations.name: Controls marketing spend
relations.description: Sets budget guardrails and spend-to-close discipline on marketing commitments, from purchase order to accrual, protecting cash and auditability.

relations.name: Sets policy and control frame
relations.description: Publishes the compliance policies, control definitions, and evidence expectations that shared-services operations must run against.

relations.name: Evidences control adherence
relations.description: Returns control-execution evidence and early variance signals so compliance and finance can prove control readiness without audit fire drills.

relations.name: Escalates product defects
relations.description: Escalates recurring defects and diagnostic context from support cases into product and engineering queues so root causes get fixed instead of re-resolved.

relations.name: Flags retention risk
relations.description: Surfaces escalation patterns and at-risk accounts from service operations to account owners before churn shows up in the forecast.

relations.name: Provides the shared platform
relations.description: Provides the enterprise platform, integration guardrails, and rationalized tooling that administrators build safe automations on.

relations.name: Automates employee workflows
relations.description: Builds and runs the safe automations, identity controls, and self-service flows that let employees complete routine requests without chasing functions.

relations.name: Raises service requests
relations.description: Submits HR, finance, procurement, and workplace requests into shared services, whose deflection and resolution performance defines the employee service experience.

relations.name: Directs and approves team work
relations.description: Assigns priorities, approves requests, and clears blockers so team members start work fast and move items through approval chains without stalls.

relations.name: Reports service and policy signals
relations.description: Feeds request throughput, policy exceptions, and onboarding status back to people managers so team capacity and new-joiner ramp stay on track.
